newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: N.Koreans meet Swiss trade, aid officials.
newsitem.headline: N.Koreans meet Swiss trade, aid officials.

text.p: North Korea's first official delegation to go abroad since a top-level defection last month started talks with Swiss diplomats on Monday, but the Berne foreign ministry said no concrete agreements were expected.
The talks included top trade and aid officials at the Swiss foreign ministry.

A ministry statement said the main issues under discussion in meetings through Wednesday would be bilateral political ties, human rights in North Korea, economic relations and possible Swiss humanitarian aid.
Switzerland has no trade or other commercial agreements with North Korea except a civil aviation treaty from 1995.
"They are here more for theoretical discussions than to make any concrete agreements," foreign ministry spokesman Livio Zanolari said.

It is the first North Korean delegation to make an official trip abroad since the defection of Pyongyang's top ideologue Hwang Jang-yop, who sought asylum at South Korea's mission to Beijing on February 12.
Analysts had said the east Asian communist country's desperate food situation was likely to be on the agenda.
